subject: EdgeFin discovery — TCO recap, levers & pilot decision criteria
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgefin.com>, David Lin <d.lin@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin discovery — TCO recap, levers & pilot decision criteria

Hi Alyssa / David —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we build the pilot TCO: 

Key pain points you called out
- Real-time transaction enrichment at scale is blowing up CPU costs in your current pipeline; latency spikes during batch settlement windows are customer-visible.
- Security/compliance requires data residency and audit logs for any external inference.
- Budget is constrained: you have a hard annual cap for inference spend for 2027 and need a predictable per-transaction unit cost.

Goals you asked us to validate
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost by 40–60% while keeping 99th pctl latency under 220ms for the critical fraud-check route.
- Provide a 3-month pilot that demonstrates unit-cost improvement, stability under peak windows, and end-to-end auditability.

Cost/TCO levers we discussed (summary)
1) Model sizing + quantization: switching to a 8-bit quantized candidate for non-sensitive paths can cut model compute by ~2.2x.
2) Batching & autoscaling: 100–300ms controlled batching windows during settlement spikes could improve throughput by ~1.6x without increasing median latency.
3) KV/prefix caching for repeat context: expected hit rates ~25–35% on typical transaction flows; reduces tokens generated per request.
4) Routing to lower-cost variant: policy-based fallbacks to a cheaper model for low-risk transactions.

Attached: a first-pass TCO workbook (EdgeFin-TCO-draft.xlsx) and a one-pager on Redwood deployment options (redwood-one-pager.pdf). The workbook has three scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive) with assumptions called out on the assumptions tab.

Open questions needed to tighten the numbers
- Exact 90/95/99 pctl latency targets for each route (you gave a 220ms target for fraud-check; is there a separate SLA for enrichment?).
- Typical tokens per request (both input and expected output) for the enrichment route and any templated prompts.
- Expected daily/weekly peak multiplier during settlement windows (you mentioned up to 4x baseline).
\Proposed next steps
1) You share token/sample payloads and a short trace of peak window traffic (anonymized) by end of week — we can use that to produce a calibrated pilot estimate.
2) Redwood delivers a pilot TCO with concrete per-transaction unit-cost, projected monthly spend, and an ops-runbook for the pilot (3 business days after we receive payloads).
3) Tentative pilot start window: Aug 17–Aug 31 (2 weeks for setup + validation).
\If this aligns, I’ll loop in our Dedicated deployment lead (Marissa) to scope infra and Ben to produce batching/cache config recommendations and expected delta to your current baseline.
\Thanks — appreciate the thoughtful questions today.
\Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EdgeFin discovery — TCO recap, levers & pilot decision criteria
\Thanks Rishi — this is helpful and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SLA: the enrichment route needs 95th pctl < 150ms; fraud-check must remain at 99th pctl < 220ms. Enrichment is our higher-volume path.
- Tokens: enrichment average ~420 input tokens and ~30 tokens output (we will send samples). Fraud-check average ~120 input / 8 output.
- Peak multiplier: settlement windows are typically 3.5–4.5x baseline for 10–15 minutes, two times per day.
- Budget: our finance lead has signaled an annual cap of $420k for inference-related SaaS/Opex in 2027; pilot should show path to at least 35% reduction vs current run rate to be considered for a larger commit.
\We will send anonymized payload samples and a synthetic peak trace by EOD Thursday. Also cc’ing procurement (David) to start flagging any special contract terms — David, can you confirm if our standard cloud vendor addendum will be sufficient or if legal needs a separate review for private deployments?
\Alyssa
Head of Product
EdgeFin

\Alyssa — quick technical follow-up on the batching/cache levers we discussed so you can share with your infra team: 

1) Batching windows: for enrichment (median input ~420 tokens) we recommend a dynamic batching policy: 50ms base micro-batch during steady state, scaling to a 150–250ms controlled latency window under high concurrency. With Redwood's continuous batching, that yields ~1.4–1.7x throughput gain depending on arrival distribution.

2) KV/prefix cache: we can precompute embeddings for static fields (merchant descriptors) and keep a warm KV cache on the serving nodes. With a 30% hit rate we remove ~120 tokens from average generation footprint (rough estimate).

3) Quantization/variant routing: Suggest running two model variants in pilot — a 8-bit quantized medium that handles enrichment, and a full-precision smaller model for high-risk fraud-checks. Routing policy: enrichment -> quantized by default; fraud-check -> full-precision unless confidence falls below threshold (then escalate).

4) Ops instrumentation we’ll deliver in pilot: token-level cost per request, batch size distribution, cache hit rates, and 90/95/99 latency by route.

I pulled some back-of-envelope numbers into the attached workbook — conservative scenario still hits ~30% unit-cost improvement; aggressive with better cache hit and batching hits 48%. Will refine once we get your traces.

—Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

\Alyssa / David — great, thanks for the confirmation and for agreeing to share traces. Quick alignment and asks before we lock pilot dates: 

1) Deliverables we will produce after we receive traces (3 business days):
   - Pilot TCO workbook (finalized numbers and scenario sensitivity).
   - Pilot configuration: model variants, batching policy, cache TTLs, routing rules.
   - Ops runbook and telemetry dashboard links (token cost, cache hit, latency percentiles).

2) Success criteria we propose for pilot acceptance:
   - >=35% reduction in per-transaction unit cost in the baseline scenario.
   - No regression in 99th pctl for fraud-check route (target < 220ms).
   - Demonstrated stable handling of 4x peak traffic without error-rate increase > 0.1%.

\3) Procurement note (David): to keep pilot friction low we can start on Redwood Hosted with a limited-data residency plan, or if you need Private we’ll scope infra cost separately. Either way, the SOW will include an SLA for uptime and audit log delivery.

If these look good I’ll send a calendar invite for an internal kickoff (30–45 min) the week of Aug 10 to align engineering and procurement. Looking forward to the traces.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
